 F01.10: Electrical Components and Craftmanship 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR4.5.1 [URS-PCS-HR-013] All wiring inside the machine must be separated into power, signal, and 
network channels.  
UR4.5.3 [URS-PCS-HR-015] All electric al components shall be UL listed.   
UR4.5.5 [MCCPDC 3.2.2] Completed, a ssembled panel shall be UL certified.  
UR4.5.6 [MCCPDC 3.2.2] Completed, assembled pan el shall be UL listed for the appropriate electrical 
area classification.  
 
Plastic wire ducting within the panel allows for the proper separation of wiring into the three 
categories: power, signal, and network cabling. 
All electrical components have been selected to carry the UL mark and are UL listed. The PCS Miscellaneous PLC panel is UL certified as indicated by its certification sticker and 
registration with UL. 
The PCS Miscellaneous PLC panel has a NEMA 4 rating.  It will be placed into Room 035 Utilities 
which has a general-purpose classification rating. 
 F01.11: Electrical Disconnect Switch 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR4.5.4 [URS-PCS-HR-016] A lockable disconnect sw itch shall be provided on each main feed to the 
PCS Miscellaneous PLC Panel enclosure.  The disconnect switch shall be rated per NEC 
guidelines of supplied voltage and current ra tings (minimum 600VAC / 30A / Non-Fused).  
 
The Allen-Bradley disconnect switch model 194E-E32-1753-6N is a lockable disconnect switch 
which meets this requirement. 
 F01.12: Stack Light (Color and Function) 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR4.6.1 [URS-PCS-HR-017] All indicator lightss hall be suitable for operation on 24VDC. Lamps (LED 
preferred) and caps shall be replaceable from  the outside front of t he panel. For lamp caps 
specified as colored in hardware design specif ications, the lamp cap colors shall be as 
follows…Stack light shall be visible from as many operating areas as possible. (see below)  
 
 UR4.6.1 [URS-PCS-HR-017] All indicator lightss hall be suitable for operation on 24VDC. Lamps (LED 
preferred) and caps shall be replacea ble from the outside front  of the panel.  For lamp caps specified as 
colored in hardware design specifications, the lamp cap colors shall be as follows (unless otherwise 
specified):  
1. Red – General meaning is “Not Operating” (e.g., motor not running, device is de-energized, valve is 
closed.).  
2. Green – General meaning is “Operating” (e.g., motor is running, device is ener gized, valve is open.).  
3. Amber – General meaning is “Warning” or “Take No te” (e.g., subsystem in mode other than normal, 
valve is in an intermediate state such as traveling between closed and open.).  
 Stack light shall be visible from as many operating areas as possible.

This function implements the following user requirement(s)

 F01.14: Audible Annunciation 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR4.8.1 [URS-PCS-HR-019] System shall have the ability to alert users with an audible alert… (see 
below)  
 
 UR4.8.1 [URS-PCS-HR-019] Alarm Modules shall:  
1. Be panel front mounted, 30mm, fully enclosed with a smooth front or stack light mounted. 
2. Have a minimum sound output of 72 dB @ 3 feet. 
3. Not de-rate the NEMA rating of the enclosure or shall be stack light mounted 
4. No be de-energized from the E-Stop circuit. 
  
 
The Allen-Bradley sounder module 856T-BP1 is 70mm (larger), stack light mounted, and has an 
output of 85 dB (louder) to alert users in the area of an alarm condition.  The mounting shall be made 
such that the NEMA rating of the enclosure is not de-rated.  As the E-Stop requirement for this 
system has been removed per RFI-001, the audible alarm is not dependent on the E-Stop circuit.

 F05.03: Print Screen Function 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR5.2.21 [URS-PCS-SR-027] The capability to generate an electronic or hard copy of any active display 
must be available via the Print Screen function.  
 
A Print Screen button visible on each display allows for the capture of that display for later review. 
 F05.04: Overview Screen 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR5.2.23 [URS-PCS-SR-029] The system shall provi de an “Overview” screen on all physical OITs. The 
overview screen will display “view-only” da ta for all critical parameters, values and 
information across the system. De tails of the required overview  information to be determined 
during detailed design.  
 
An Overview Screen (Main) is provided which displays the critical parameters, values, and 
information as described in Section 3.1.12 Overview Screen below.  
 
 F05.05: Input State and Simulation Review Screen 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR5.3.3 [URS-PCS-SR-032] All inputs shall provide st ate and simulation features . This shall be captured 
on a separate maintenance screen, accessible by Admin and Maintenance personnel.  
 
An Input State and Simulation Review screens are present which are only accessible to the 
Administrator and Maintenance login security levels.  These screens displays the state of the wired input (actual input) and the state of the simulated input and if the simulation function is active for that particular input (simulated state is what controller sees).    
Since an Administrator or Maintenance person may put any input point in SIMULATE and change its 
value, it is the responsibility of this person to supervise and adjust the manually inserted value for any 
points placed in SIMULATE.  Failure to properly supervise and adjust manually inserted values may cause incorrect control functions and may lead to equipment damage. 
 F05.06: PLC firmware version and OIT version available via HMI 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR5.2.17 [USR-PCS-SR-023] The PLC revision will be addressed to a PLC register, and hard coded OIT 
revision shall be accessible via a main menu  selection to users with Administrator or 
Engineer security level privileges.

F05.00: SCADA Proc ess Visualization 
The FactoryTalk View SE HMI enables operators and production personnel to view and monitor the 
process.  Visualization of the process is established through different screens that show the important 
process data and critical process parameters.   
  
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR5.2.9 [URS-PCS-SR-015] The system shall provide display of analog signal status, numerical values, 
engineering units, and alarming.   
UR5.2.18 [URS-PCS-SR-024] All soft key buttons shall be  of sufficient size to allow finger touch of the 
object to activate it and have adequate space between objects to ensure the correct object 
is being selected.  Soft key button sizing and locations shall be approved during design 
review.  The OIT shall provide a mechanism to confirm operator actions (e.g., pop-up 
window, etc.).   
 
 The FactoryTalk View SE HMI satisfies the requirements for a method to display the values 
described as well as a method to generate pop-up windows.  Guidelines for colors, font sizes, graphics to use, and more are discussed in the HMI programming specification (reference document [10]).

 F05.01: Trending 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR5.2.19 [URS-PCS-SR-025] Real-time multi-pen trends  for all analog and defined discrete signals.  Also, 
PID loop controller screens to include trending for PV, SP and CV as applicable.  
 
The system provides the ability to trend any of the tags in the PCS-CP01 PLC controller which 
includes both analog and discrete signals.  Tags can be added and removed at runtime.  The 
trending requirement for the PV, SP, and CV of the PID loops does not apply since there are no PID 
loops under the control of the PCS-CP01 system.   
 F05.02: Display colors of dynamic objects 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR5.2.20 [URS-PCS-SR-026] The following colors shall be utilized when indicat ing states of dynamic 
objects…(see below)  
 
The following colors shall be utilized when indicating states of dynamic objects:  1. Gray – General meaning is “Not Operating” (e.g., motor not running, device is de-
energized, valve is closed).  
2. Green – General meaning is “Operating” (e.g., motor is running, device is energized, 
valve is open.). 
3. Yellow – General meaning is “Warning” or “Take Note” (e.g., device is in a mode 
other than normal such as manual mode, valve is in an intermediate state such as 
manual mode, valve is in an intermediate state such as traveling between closed and open).  
4. Red – General meaning is “Alarm” or “Lockout” (e.g., an alarm is active on a device or 
Operation, lockout is activated).  
The color palette is applied to dynamic objects to reflect the colors shown above.

Both Microsoft Windows domain security and the FactoryTalk System Administration tool can enable the 
creation of a unique login and password for each user. 
FactoryTalk View SE can use Microsoft Windows security to manage user accounts. Password 
expiration, password aging, password complexity  requirements, account expiration, disabling of 
accounts, lockout aftern invalid login attempts, and forcing a change of password on first login are all security features provided by both Microso ft Windows security and FactoryTalk Security. 
Procedures should be implemented to ensure that user IDs do not get deleted or reassigned.  It is 
recommended to disable user IDs rather than deleting them as a best practice. 
The customer’s management procedure should include the verification of the identity of an individual 
before sanctioning an individual’s electronic signature. 
Once a user has been sanctioned and a unique account with password has been created in the 
FactoryTalk View SE system, the user is required to enter his/ her login and password to access FactoryTalk View SE. This process validates the identity of the user to FactoryTalk View SE. 
FactoryTalk View SE requires two components for us er identification: a unique login ID and password. 
When using the FactoryTalk View SE electronic signature feature, both the user login ID and password 
are required to perform an action.  The FactoryTalk View SE electronic signature feature can be configured to display and record the meaning of the signature. It also allows for separate performer and approval signatures, and for comments to be added regarding the meaning of the signature. 
If the user logs out of FactoryTalk View SE and again requires access, the user must reenter the login ID 
and password.

F09.00: Physical Security 
It is essential to limit operator access to  the hardware running Windows operating systems and 
FactoryTalk View SE.  In general, an operator’s only access to the computer should be via the keyboard, mouse, or touch screen.  An operator with access to the power switch and bootable media 
could have direct access to the underlying file syst em and could potentially circumvent many of the 
security measures described in this document.  It is the responsibility of the Mark Cuban Cost Plus 
Drug Company, PBC. to put measures in place to limit operator access and to protect the hardware systems.

 F10.01: System Security Configuration 
Security is used to restrict a user’s access to certain parts of the system.  FactoryTalk View SE uses a 
combination of Microsoft Windows domain security and FactoryTalk View SE security.  While Windows security is used to authenticate users and restrict operating system level actions, FactoryTalk View SE runtime security restricts graphical user interface access and control system function access.  The 
FactoryTalk View SE security is based on a system of letter codes (A-P) which are assigned to the 
individual users to define their access.

 F10.02: FactoryTalk View SE Security 
 Use a password-protected screen saver.  To ensure that only operators with the proper 
credentials are accessing workstations in a closed system, a password-protected screen 
saver can be used on the FactoryTalk View SE Client terminals.  This system will take the recommended exception to this rule when critical process data must be displayed at all times.  In this case, a ‘view only’ user account will be logged in to display the status of production and alarm information.  
 Use the included DeskLock software feature to restrict operators’ access to the client’s 
operating system.  
 Disable switch to other applications since this opens access to other programs.  
 Disable ‘Allow display code debugging’  since this allows launching of the VBA editor, 
which is not secure. 
 Change the window properties of the FactoryTalk View SE Client to disable the title 
bar, the system menu, the close button, and the show diagnostics list.  Set the window to be maximized. 
 F10.03: Configure FactoryTalk View SE clients automatically login as DEFAULT user 
after a period of inactivity 
Since the system requires that critical operations  information be displayed at all times, the DEFAULT 
User (a user with ‘view only’ access) shall be logged in when a period of inactivity occurs.  This allows the read-only display of production and alarm information.  
FactoryTalk View SE clients can be configured to automatically log out after a specified 
period of time, however this feature does not subsequently permit the immediate and automatic login of another user (DEFAULT) as required.  To achieve the required actions, idle conditions will be detected and then the DEFAULT user will be logged in effectively logging out the current user.

The Rockwell Software Factory Talk View SE platform shall be configured to make use of electronic 
signature features.  The delivered system has the Rockwell Software FactoryTalk View SE software loaded onto it, which hosts an operator interface application.  The delivered system has a custom operator interface application written for monitoring and, where appropriate, controlling the connected systems. 
 
The control system is programmed using control modules and follows the S88/S95 standards as 
applicable.  Process sequences have been programmed with steps and transitions as required, based on 
descriptions in the control logic narratives.   
 The Rockwell Software FactoryTalk View SE platform provides the ability to archive continuous process data, alarms, alarm acknowledgement, events, parameters, and ancillary data.  The alarm and events service saves all alarms and events in Universal Coordinated Time (UTC) 
without any time zone offsets or daylight savings adjustments added.  When the events are retrieved 
from the database for viewing, local time zone offsets or daylight savings adjustments can be applied.  In this way, the system does not lose any accuracy or data due to daylight savings or time zone offsets.    
The FactoryTalk Historian system reads data from the PCS-CP01 PLC and logs it appropriately. 
 The operator interface text will be displayed in English.
